edges.mechanism: Labels declare fish (shark) ingredients; fish collagen/gelatin is a recognized fish allergen (21% of fish-allergic patients sensitized) and fish-collagen tablets have caused anaphylaxis. Shark (cartilaginous) cross-reactivity is lower but not absent.
edges.evidence: Product label; allergen cohort studies, case report, molecular review; no challenge data with Viviscal itself

edges.mechanism: Labels declare mollusc (oyster extract) content; oyster tropomyosin (Cra g 1) is the main mollusc allergen and cross-reacts across molluscs.
edges.evidence: Product label plus allergen reviews; no product-specific challenge data

edges.mechanism: Biotin component (about 240 mcg/day in the women's formula) can falsely lower streptavidin-biotin troponin assays; FDA reported a death after a falsely low troponin with high-dose biotin. Risk at Viviscal's dose alone is probably low except on the most sensitive assays (Ortho TnI threshold 2.5 ug/L); higher when stacked with other biotin products.
edges.evidence: FDA safety communication (report), real-world prevalence and risk-model studies; no serum biotin data at Viviscal dose

edges.mechanism: Biotin falsely lowers TSH/thyroglobulin (sandwich assays) and raises FT4/FT3 (competitive assays), mimicking Graves' disease; shown at 10 mg/day with peak 2 h post-dose. Platform-dependent.
edges.evidence: Prospective dosing study, case reports with literature review, 2026 ETA guideline

edges.with: biotin-streptavidin immunoassays (hormones, ferritin, vitamin D, B12, PTH, PSA, NT-proBNP)
edges.mechanism: Biotin interference in other immunoassays; newer reagents tolerate 1000-3000 ng/mL, older ones less. Disclose biotin intake to the laboratory.
edges.evidence: Analytical spiking studies and reviews

edges.mechanism: Additive biotin from B-complex or hair/skin/nail products raises cumulative biotin and the chance of immunoassay interference.
edges.evidence: Inferred from dose-dependent interference data

edges.mechanism: Iron (20 mg/day) and calcium (120 mg/day) in the formula chelate/adsorb levothyroxine and reduce absorption; ferrous sulfate caused hypothyroidism, persisting in one case despite 4 h separation. Separate doses and check TSH.
edges.evidence: Case reports, prospective calcium study (TSH 1.6 to 2.7 mIU/L), PK crossover (20-25% lower absorption); doses in Viviscal lower than in studies

edges.mechanism: Calcium, iron and zinc chelate quinolones and reduce antibiotic absorption; separate dosing.
edges.evidence: Pharmacokinetic interaction review

edges.mechanism: Iron and calcium salts chelate tetracyclines, reducing absorption by 50-90%; a 3-hour interval prevents the interaction.
edges.evidence: Pharmacokinetic review

edges.mechanism: Viviscal supplies about 22 mg/day zinc (near EFSA UL 25 mg); adding a zinc supplement can exceed ULs and cause zinc-induced copper deficiency (anemia, neutropenia, neuropathy), often undiagnosed.
edges.evidence: Toxicology review and case series from a trace-element laboratory

edges.mechanism: Cumulative iron intake (Viviscal 20 mg/day non-heme iron); no evidence that iron helps hair without documented deficiency; raises overload risk in susceptible people.
edges.evidence: Reviews; no interaction study

edges.mechanism: Supplemental iron plus vitamin C (which enhances non-heme iron absorption) works against the management goal of keeping ferritin low by phlebotomy.
edges.evidence: Management guidance plus absorption reviews; inference

edges.mechanism: Viviscal contains about 118 mg/day vitamin C; extra vitamin C further enhances non-heme iron absorption from meals, though the effect over a full diet is small.
edges.evidence: Iron-absorption studies

edges.mechanism: Phenolic-rich green tea extract reduced non-heme iron absorption (12.1% to 8.9%); may blunt the iron component if co-ingested.
edges.evidence: Isotope-labelled meal study in women

edges.mechanism: Duplicates the marine collagen component; fish-derived collagen peptides are a fish allergen and have their own hair-diameter RCT data.
edges.evidence: One RCT plus allergen cohort; no combination study

edges.mechanism: Horsetail (Equisetum arvense) is diuretic (comparable to HCTZ) and lowered BP at 900 mg/day; Viviscal contains only 25-73 mg/day, so additive effect is theoretical.
edges.evidence: Two small RCTs of horsetail extract; dose far above Viviscal's

edges.mechanism: Theoretical: horsetail's diuretic effect could alter lithium clearance; no case reports or studies found at Viviscal's low horsetail dose.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference only from horsetail diuretic RCT

edges.mechanism: Label states the product is not intended for pregnant or nursing women or under-18s; no safety data exist.
edges.evidence: Label precaution only

edges.mechanism: Iron-containing tablets are a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6; keep out of reach.
edges.evidence: Label warning; population-based case-control study

edges.with: hair loss with nutritional deficiency (iron, zinc)
edges.mechanism: Micronutrient components are most plausibly helpful when deficiency exists; TE is linked to low ferritin and vitamin D, AA to low zinc. Test and treat the cause rather than supplementing blindly.
edges.evidence: Meta-analyses of observational data, reviews
